edits.html:
Which vaccine prevents it Face-first maculopapular rash that spreads down — measles or rubella; the MMR (measles, mumps and rubella) vaccine prevents both · Schedule — MMR is a live attenuated vaccine given in 2 doses, at 12 to 15 months and at 4 to 6 years · Itching — mild itching does not make a rash varicella; varicella needs vesicles in crops
How NBME framed it The lead-in asked which vaccine would have prevented the rash, so MMR was the answer whether the illness was measles or rubella. The options listed the routine childhood vaccines plus one travel vaccine, typhoid.
edits.note: Q12: prevention task; MMR covers measles and rubella; NBME framing

edits.anchor: day care and a single vaccine dose explain all the findings.
edits.html:
True-fact-wrong-slotDiphtheria-tetanus-acellular pertussis vaccine: a routine childhood vaccine that a recent immigrant may have missed; diphtheria, tetanus and pertussis do not cause a spreading maculopapular rash.
True-fact-wrong-slotHaemophilus influenzae type b vaccine: another routine vaccine she may have missed; this organism causes epiglottitis, meningitis and pneumonia, not a face-first rash.
True-fact-wrong-slotHepatitis B vaccine: a routine infant vaccine she may have missed; acute hepatitis B brings right upper quadrant pain and nausea, and she has no abdominal symptoms.
True-fact-wrong-slotInactivated poliovirus vaccine: a routine vaccine she may have missed abroad; polio causes flaccid paralysis, not a rash.
True-fact-wrong-slotPneumococcal vaccine: a routine childhood vaccine she may have missed; pneumococcus causes otitis media, pneumonia and meningitis, not a viral exanthem.
Unchecked attributeInfluenza vaccine: fever, fatigue and a runny nose fit influenza; influenza does not typically cause a rash.
Salient decoyTyphoid vaccine: fever and a rash in a child from Central America suggest typhoid rose spots; she has no abdominal pain or diarrhea, and her rash began on the face and covers the whole body.
Unchecked attributeVaricella vaccine: itching and a whole-body rash suggest chickenpox; her lesions are discrete maculopapules with no vesicles.
edits.note: Q12: one trap line per NBME distractor

edits.stem: 10 yo F who recently immigrated from Central America, vaccine history not given; 5 days of low-grade fever, fatigue, mild itching and a mild runny nose, then 1 day of a rash that began on the face and now covers the body; no abdominal pain or diarrhea; T 37.8 C; discrete maculopapular lesions on the face, trunk, back and limbs; no eye or mouth lesions
edits.companion: it prevents both measles and rubella; the low fever, discrete spots and absent conjunctivitis fit rubella better than measles
edits.lead_in: Which of the following vaccines is most likely to have prevented this patient's condition?

edits.stem: 7 yo F who recently moved from abroad with no vaccine records; 2 days of low-grade fever and a mild runny nose, then pink, discrete maculopapular spots that began on the face and spread to the trunk and limbs within a day; well-appearing; T 37.9 C; tender posterior auricular and suboccipital nodes; eyes and buccal mucosa normal
edits.companion: mild illness with posterior nodes; the MMR vaccine prevents it
